back: Plan Financial Management, Estimate Costs, Develop Budget, Monitor and Control Finances.
Evaluate performance, track spending, show accountability, inform stakeholders, forecast, evaluate return, support risk management.
Tangible value (ROI, IRR, payback, ROA, ROACE), social or environmental value, and intangible value such as satisfaction and innovation.
CapEx: invested in physical assets (buildings, equipment, technology). OpEx: running costs (wages, rent, utilities, administration).
The budget, plus the type of money (CapEx, OpEx), a set purpose, or a period such as a fiscal year.
Financial management plan and funding strategy.
Fixed or reallocated internal budgets, lump sum, incremental disbursement, external investment, government or NGO grants.
Acquiring funding, often from outside for long-term infrastructure and public projects; the funder may set requirements.
Cost estimates, basis of estimates, document updates (assumption log, lessons learned, risk register).
Uses actual values from a similar past project; quick and cheap, but less accurate.
An algorithm on historical data and parameters, such as cost per square meter.
Estimates the lowest-level work and aggregates it up the WBS; the most detailed.
(Optimistic + Most likely + Pessimistic) / 3.
Rough order of magnitude: −25% to +75%. Definitive: −5% to +10%.
Checks whether the schedule and budget reserve is sufficient for the remaining risk.
For identified risks (known-unknowns); usually inside the cost baseline; may be used, reduced or eliminated as risks pass.
For unforeseen work within scope (unknown-unknowns); outside the cost baseline; usually released by senior management.
The amount used is added to the cost baseline, which needs an approved change.
Work estimates + contingency reserve = cost baseline; + management reserve = project budget.
The approved, time-phased budget, excluding management reserve, changed only through formal change control.
Total and periodic funding derived from the cost baseline; total funds = cost baseline + management reserve.
Compares planned spending with funding limits; may reschedule work to level the rate of spending.
The WBS component used for cost accounting, with a code linked to the accounting system.
Work performance information, revenue and cost forecasts, change requests, funding proposals, plan and document updates.
The spent curve is flatter; budgets may be set per quarter and revised; time-phased budgeting and continuous funding assessment.
